children: Oman and Angola have moved to broaden their economic and investment partnership, with a two-day state visit by His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik resulting in new cooperation across energy, mining, logistics, agriculture, fisheries and transport.
The visit to Luanda on September 17 and 18 brought the two countries’ economic ambitions into sharper focus, with agreements and memoranda signed during the visit valued at more than US$1.5bn.

Speaking during the visit, His Majesty the Sultan said the current level of trade between Oman and Angola did not yet reflect the strength of their economic relationship and called for efforts to substantially increase trade in coming years. He also urged public and private sector institutions in both countries to pursue investment opportunities emerging from the partnership.
The state visit, made at the invitation of Angolan President João Manuel Lourenço, was aimed at translating the closer political dialogue between the two countries into wider economic engagement.

The two leaders held a private meeting at the Presidential Palace in Luanda, followed by expanded official talks. The discussions covered industry, mining, energy, clean energy, ports, maritime transport, logistics, agriculture, food security and fisheries.

President Lourenço said the visit marked an advanced stage in expanding the countries’ economic, investment and commercial partnership. He pointed to the opening of the African Bank of Oman in Luanda this year and the entry of Omani companies into mineral mining investments in Angola as examples of growing cooperation.
He also identified agriculture, fisheries, mineral resources, oil and gas and pharmaceutical manufacturing as areas where further opportunities could be developed for private investors.

title: ZAWYA: Oman, Angola open new chapter in economic and investment partnership
